subject: Senior signoff request: Hosted API onboarding discount for Venturelane
messages:
From: Evan Lowe <evan@venturelane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pilot + pricing ask

Kim —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move forward with a 6‑month pilot that will ingest live traffic for our support assistant. Our procurement team is reviewing the SOW but asked whether Redwood can provide a deeper onboarding/early‑ramp discount on Hosted API usage — ideally in the 25% range for the first 12 months — to make the economics feasible for our board.

I attached an initial usage forecast so you can see the expected ramp. Can we get a sense of whether that kind of concession is possible and what approvals are needed? Evan

Attachments: Venturelane_SOW_v1.pdf; venturelane_usage_forecast.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Evan Lowe <evan@venturelane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pilot + pricing ask

Evan —

Appreciate the context and the forecast. Short answer: concessions above our standard tiered discounts require senior approval. I’ve looped in Ben (deal desk) and Marcus (commercial) to scope the request.

Next steps from our side: Ben will review the forecast and propose a concession structure. If we recommend >20% we’ll need an exec signoff and a written amendment to the SOW. Can you confirm the committed monthly minimum you’d be willing to commit to during the 12 months? That number will materially affect the approval rationale.

I attached your forecast and SOW to our internal thread for review.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | (415) 555‑0192
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pilot + pricing ask

Team —

I reviewed the forecast. Venturelane is early but shows a clean enterprise product and a likely multi‑region expansion in Q2 next year. Their forecast is modest initially (~2M tokens / mo rising to 20M by month 9). The SOW calls for pilot support and a single model (L2) hosted in us‑west.

Recommendation: Offer a structured concession — 24% off list Hosted API usage for the first 12 months in exchange for: 1) a 12‑month committed monthly minimum of 4M tokens (billed monthly), 2) a clause that re‑prices to standard rates if they miss two consecutive months of committed usage, and 3) joint case study permission. We should also cap the concession to the specified model class.

Rationale: 24% gets us above standard renew/early ramp bands to win strategic reference business without creating long tail precedent if we tie to firm commitments and a review clause. Approving >20% requires Marcus’ signoff.

I’m attaching a redline SOW excerpt and a short AM playbook for legal/finance handoff.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pilot + pricing ask

Ben —

Thanks for the detail. A few product/finance notes before we escalate: 1) If we give 24% without limiting model variants, the realized cost could exceed expectations if they switch to larger context models. Suggest language restricting to the L2 baseline and requiring notice for model changes. 2) From a revenue recognition standpoint, a committed MRR with usage true‑up is fine but legal needs clear amendment language. 3) Recommend a 6‑month operational review (metrics: latency, token efficiency, cache hit rate) and an automatic re‑contract window — that will protect performance and ROI.

If leadership prefers a cleaner approval route, a 20% signoff today with a 3‑month performance checkpoint could be acceptable. But since the customer is asking for 25%, I support Ben’s structure if Marcus is comfortable with the precedent.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Lowe <evan@venturelane.com>, procure@venturelane.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting senior approval: Venturelane onboarding concession (25% ask)

Marcus —

Recap: Venturelane is requesting a 25% discount for the first 12 months to make the pilot board‑approved. Ben’s recommended concession is 24% with a 12‑month MCM of 4M tokens and program controls (model restriction, re‑price on underuse, case study). Mina flagged product and finance controls and proposed a 6‑month operational review.

Why approve: Venturelane is a strategic reference target in the talent‑sourcing vertical and is likely to expand into EU/EMEA in H2 2027; landing them would materially help our vertical play and provide a strong case study. Losing the concession likely kills the deal given their board economics.

Ask: Please approve up to a 25% onboarding concession for Hosted API usage for 12 months, subject to legal amendment and the conditions Ben outlined. If you prefer a reduced figure, please advise the maximum % you’ll authorize and any additional conditions (finance/legal handoffs). I have a DocuSign envelope ready and the customer is standing by.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redline_SOW_excerpt.pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Requesting senior approval: Venturelane onboarding concession (25% ask)

Team —

Understood and thank you for the crisp summary. I approve a concession above our standard bands but will cap the onboarding discount at 22% for the first 12 months, contingent on the following conditions being met before signature: 1) Legal to approve and sign an amendment that restricts the concession to the named L2 model and includes the underuse re‑price clause Ben suggested; 2) Finance to sign off on the committed monthly minimum billing and revenue recognition language; 3) A 6‑month operational review with automatic renegotiation trigger if key metrics aren’t met; 4) Customer commits to a public reference/case study.

If the customer will not accept 22% we’ll revert to the standard 20% pilot concession and present that as a final offer. Kimberly — please coordinate legal/finance immediately and update the DocuSign envelope with the amendment; copy me on the final.

Marcus Lin
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
